hints: Focus on the word hybridoma. What two cell types are fused together at the start, and what is selected afterwards?
Remember monoclonal means one type of antibody from one type of cell. What must you grow many identical copies of to keep making that exact same antibody?
walkthrough:
**Recall what a hybridoma is**

Think of it as a super-cell made by fusion. A B-lymphocyte that makes the right antibody is fused with a myeloma (cancer) cell that divides forever.

That fused cell is called a hybridoma.

**Why we need to select and copy one cell**

Not every fusion works, so scientists test and pick out the single hybridoma that makes exactly the wanted antibody. That one cell is then allowed to divide to make a large population of genetically identical cells.

**Link to monoclonal antibodies**

Identical cells make identical antibodies. Growing that identical population by cell culture gives a continuous supply of one type, or monoclonal, antibody. That identical population is called clones.

options.A: Antigens are used at the start to immunise the mouse, but they are not grown in culture to make the antibodies.
options.B: Correct. The selected hybridoma is grown into clones, identical cells that all secrete the same monoclonal antibody.
options.C: Lymphocytes alone cannot be grown long term in culture as they die, which is why they must first be fused to form hybridomas.
options.D: Myeloma cells provide the ability to divide forever, but on their own they do not make the wanted antibody.
